intro: Before you rise the Manazan Caves, a rock settlement in Karaman province from the 4th–9th century AD. It is cut five storeys into a valley wall; its stairs run inside the rock, and its top floor can be reached only from within.
history: Under Byzantium, this settlement, cut five storeys into a valley wall, served as both shelter and store. Its stairs run inside the rock and the top floor can be reached only from within — an arrangement that leaves it all but unreachable from outside.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the five-storey rock settlement and its internal stairs, then look for the storage rooms and the rock faces.
facts: Did you know? Bodies preserved by the dry cave air are known as the Manazan mummies, and they gave the site its reputation. The settlement is cut five storeys into a valley wall, and its top floor can be reached only from within.
outro: This brings our journey through the Manazan Caves to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
